review.finding: coverage.thresholds.global is a glob key that matches no file, so the 80% gate is not enforced. This predates the change: global is Jest syntax and has been a no-op since vitest 1.
review.suggestion: Fix it in a separate iterate (flatten the thresholds) so the change in behaviour gets its own trace. [Implementer: deferred, reported to the operator.]

review.finding: vitest 5 needs vite ^6.4.0 as a peer, but the manifest still allowed ^6.3.5. The lockfile already resolves 6.4.5.
review.suggestion: Raise the floor to ^6.4.0. [Implementer: applied; the lockfile resolution is unchanged.]

review.finding: Nothing states the new Node minimum: there is no engines field and no .nvmrc.
review.suggestion: Optionally add engines >=22.12 or a .nvmrc. Not blocking. [Implementer: deferred, reported.]

notes: The vitest.config options are all still valid on v5, and none of the removed options are used. The v4+ restoreAllMocks semantics were checked across every test that relies on it, and no test passes for the wrong reason. The @vitest-environment node docblocks, vi.hoisted and fake timers are fine. Only test.yml names a Node version. Parameters<typeof fetch>[0] is equivalent to RequestInfo | URL. The jest-dom/vitest entry is the documented import.
